description: Self-levelling, ultra quickhardening smoothing compound for thicknesses from 1 to 10 mm per coat
whereToUse: Ultraplan Contract, especially suitable for the large building site, is used in interiors for levelling and smoothing differences in thicknesses from 1 to 10 mm on new or existing substrates, preparing them to receive all kinds of flooring where high resistance to loads and traffic is required.
Levelling concrete slabs and cementitious screeds or Topcem or Topcem Pronto based screeds.
Levelling existing concrete pavements, terrazzo, ceramic and natural stone floors.
notFor: Do not use Ultraplan Contract for exterior applications.
Do not use Ultraplan Contract on substrates subject to continuous rising damp.
Do not apply Ultraplan Contract at temperatures below +5°C.
Do not apply Ultraplan Contract in thicknesses less than 3 mm when wooden flooring needs to be installed.

mixing: While mixing with a low-speed mixer, pour in a container containing 5-5.25 L (20-21%) of clean water a 25 kg bag of Ultraplan Contract to obtain a homogeneous, lump-free mix.
packaging: Ultraplan Contract is available in 25 kg bags.
storage: Ultraplan Contract in its original unopened packaging and in a dry place, can be stored for 12 months.
notes: POT LIFE INCONSISTENCY: the technical data table gives 'Pot life: 20-35 min' while the mixing section says to prepare a quantity that can be applied within 20-30 minutes (at +23°C). STRENGTH ROWS: the compressive and flexural rows each have three sub-rows; they are copied as one label and one value string in the order printed, so compressive is 12 MPa after 1 day, 20 MPa after 7 days, 30 MPa after 28 days and flexural is 3 MPa after 1 day, 5 MPa after 7 days, 6 MPa after 28 days (these combined strings match the reading-order text file; in the layout file each value sits beside its own sub-row). The row '- Resilient and wood flooring' is a sub-row of 'Waiting time before application of the covering'. CONSUMPTION: one figure only (1.7 kg/m² per mm of thickness). For thicknesses greater than 10 mm (max. 20 mm) the sheet recommends adding approximately 20-30% of sand with a grain size of 0/4 or 0/8 but gives no consumption figure for that extended mix. The description prints 'quickhardening' as one word in both text files (probably 'quick-hardening' with the hyphen lost); copied as found. No EN 13813 class is stated in this sheet; EMICODE EC1 Plus is mentioned in the body text only, not in the table. The table gives an application temperature range up to +40°C. Minimum thickness is 3 mm when wooden flooring is to be installed. Water per bag (5-5.25 L per 25 kg) agrees with 20-21%. Primer G dilution in this sheet is 1:1 with water on dusty or particularly porous concrete.
